story_text:
## Introducing Altar II
A shockingly thin, fully mechanical keyboard. Altar II combines a superlative typing experience with an unbelievable design.
## Design goals
The designer of Altar II discusses some of the design goals, background and difficulties of making Altar II a reality.
## Hands-on demo
A brief overview of some Altar II functionality. Here it is shown pairing over Bluetooth and working with Sanctuary™, its native macOS companion app. We demonstrate using M-Dial™, remapping keys, and more, and give a general tour of the app. Shown on engineering prototype hardware with pre-alpha software and firmware.
## Mechanical switches
The strikingly slim profile is enabled by breakthrough mechanical switch design — a dual steel-armed switch with a laterally arranged spring and 40gf actuation force.
## — Mechanical switches
## Remarkably thin
At 4.75mm, Altar II is the thinnest production mechanical keyboard ever made.
## — Comparison
## Meet M-Dial™
A magnetically detachable, clickable, swappable dial for volume, media and other controls. Two sizes of M-Dial™ are included in the box: Standard issue and low-profile.
## — M-Dial™
## Haptic feedback
A haptic driver called Harmonic Synthesiser™ adds subtle physical feedback to typing, dial rotation, and keyboard state changes.
## — Haptic feedback
## Native macOS app
A fully native, Swift-based companion app for macOS gives full control over key mapping, backlight, haptics, audio and M-Dial™ functionality. Its lickable UI feels right at home on Mac.
## — Made for Mac
## Sleep-preserving backlight
NiteLite™ is a red backlight that preserves night vision, and reduces eye strain by avoiding the blue light used in most keyboard backlights.
## — Backlight
## Acoustic and vibration damping
A two-layer Inertial Damper™ system isolates the typing platform and gives Altar II a unique typing sound and feel.
## Design
Every element of Altar II — key shape, layout, typography, materials, footprint — is painstakingly designed, down to the last detail.
## Ergonomics
Altar II's slimline chassis keeps wrists almost flat during typing, reducing the strain associated with most keyboards, and negating the need for angling the typing platform.
## Technology
Fitting a full mechanical keyboard, battery, haptic system, speaker, and wireless radio into a sub-5mm chassis required bleeding-edge engineering and effort.
## Sustainability
Altar II is made from recycled plastic and recyclable aluminium, and ships in completely plastic-free packaging.
## — Sustainability
## Power
Up to 30 days of typical use on a single charge, with two days of usage from two minutes of charging over USB-C.
## In the box
Altar II keyboard, coiled USB-C cable, two M-Dials (standard issue and low profile), field manual, and EMO stickers.
## Typing test
Recorded on pre-production hardware with Zoom H5, 24-bit/48kHz, XY stereo, 40cm above device, 80Hz high-pass.
## Technical specification
- Height — 4.75mm
- Width — 299mm
- Depth — 116.5mm
- Firmware — ZMK, Zephyr-based real-time operating system (RTOS)
- Switches — Dual steel arm scissor switch w/ retention spring, 40gf actuation force
- Materials — REGEN polymer, 6061 aluminium, TPU footpad, silicone membrane, FR4 logic board
- Battery life — Up to 30-day battery life with normal use
- Connectivity — 2× Bluetooth 5.0 Low Energy (LE) channels, 1× USB-C
- OS support — Apple macOS 12 (Monterey) and up, Microsoft Windows 10 and up, Linux
- Typefaces — Tobias by Displaay Type Foundry, GT Flexa by Grilli Type
- Companion app compat. — macOS 26 Tahoe and up
## Rewards
## Add-ons
## Shipping
We ship Altar II almost anywhere. To see an estimated shipping cost, choose your country after selecting a reward.
You pay nothing for shipping today. Closer to shipping we will send every backer a survey to confirm your address and keyboard layout. Shipping and any applicable taxes are charged after the survey, when Altar II is ready to ship.
Wherever we can, we will collect VAT, GST or sales tax together with your shipping, so there is nothing to pay on delivery. In some countries, import duties and taxes are charged on delivery and are the backer's responsibility. We will confirm the arrangements for your country before anything is charged. Our aim is to avoid any duties or taxes being charged on delivery.
The estimated delivery for Altar II is July 2027. Our aim is to begin shipping in June 2027 and have completed fulfilment by August 2027. If anything changes, you will hear it from us first, in a Kickstarter update and via our newsletter.
Further detail can be found in the FAQ.
## Timeline
## About Electronic Materials Office®
Electronic Materials Office®, also known as EMO®, is a future-oriented consumer hardware corporation based in London, United Kingdom.
## Altar I
Altar I, EMO’s debut product, completely sold out in its first run, won a Red Dot Design Award, and was featured in publications like Forbes and Eurogamer.
## EMO® Manifesto
01. The world is fucked unless we, collectively, do something about it.
02. Sustainability is luxury.
03. Everything in black.
04. Well paid workers. Good working conditions.
05. Simply + thoughtfully designed.
06. Made for longevity.
risks: Altar II is the second mechanical keyboard from Electronic Materials Office®. We successfully delivered our first product, Altar I, to customers in 2024. Everything we learned shipping that product has been applied to Altar II. Hardware involves real risk. Component availability, supply chain disruptions, and global events can all affect timelines. We have built buffers into our schedule and have partnered with established manufacturers who have decades of experience bringing complex consumer hardware to market. They have been involved in the design process to ensure a smooth transition to production. We have also deliberately delayed this campaign until production tooling was underway and the design was production-ready. Our in-house team has worked hard to create a robust, manufacturable, durable product. If there are complications or delays, you will hear it from us directly. We will publish updates on a regular cadence — even when there is no major news, and will be open and honest about anything we encounter.

faq.q: How do I back Altar II on Kickstarter?
faq.a:
1. Sign in to your Kickstarter account, or create one if you haven’t already.
2. Click “back this project” at the top of the Altar II campaign page, or click a reward tier.
3. Choose your shipping country.
4. Review your pledge summary, enter your payment details and click “pledge”.

If you reserved Altar II prior to the campaign, open the link you received in your inbox instead to make sure you get the reservation price.

faq.q: I reserved Altar II before the campaign, how do I claim my reservation price?
faq.a:
To claim the reservation price, open the link in the email we sent you when the campaign launched. The link works until the campaign ends on 10 December 2026.

Note that to take advantage of the reservation price, you must have made a reservation prior to the campaign launch on Kickstarter on 10 November 2026.

faq.q: I can't find my reservation email. What should I do?
faq.a: Please check your spam or junk folder. If you still can't find it, email us at mail@electronicmaterialsoffice.com with the name, date and last four digits of the card you reserved with, and we'll take care of this for you.

faq.q: My Kickstarter email is different from my reservation email. Is that OK?
faq.a: It is fine if your Kickstarter email address and reservation email address are different. Simply open the link from your reservation email and log in to Kickstarter as normal.

faq.q: Can I pledge more than one Altar II?
faq.a: You can pledge up to two Altar II keyboards. To do this, choose a reward for your first keyboard, then add "Additional Altar II" to your pledge. Both keyboards ship together in one parcel.

faq.q: How do I change my pledge?
faq.a: You can change your pledge during the campaign by visiting the project page and clicking “manage your pledge”. On the next page choose “change your pledge” and then change your pledge amount.

Kickstarter charges your card when the campaign ends on 10 December 2026, and only if the campaign reaches its goal.

Taxes and shipping will be charged at a later date, when we are ready to ship Altar II.

faq.q: What happens after the campaign ends?
faq.a:
When the campaign ends, Kickstarter will process your pledge amount and charge you.

Closer to shipping time, we will send everyone a survey via email. This survey will ask you to confirm your shipping address, layout preference, and any other details we need to process your order.

After you fill out this survey, you will be charged the shipping fees and any taxes on your order. Both depend on your address.

Shipping is expected around July 2027. US orders are planned to be fulfilled from a US…

faq.q: How will VAT, GST, or import taxes work?
faq.a:
For the UK, EU, Australia and the US, any VAT, GST or sales tax will be charged together with shipping fees, prior to shipping of Altar II. This is to ensure there is nothing to pay on delivery.

In some countries, such as Canada, Japan, Switzerland, Norway and Republic of Korea, local import duties and taxes may be charged on delivery. We will endeavour to avoid this wherever possible.

In all other countries, local import duties and taxes are charged on delivery and are the responsibility of t…

faq.q: I missed the campaign. Can I still back Altar II?
faq.a: Late pledges will be open at $329 from the end of the campaign until Altar II is shipped to backers.

faq.q: How much will Altar II cost after Kickstarter?
faq.a:
Altar II will retail at $349. This price comes into effect when Altar II has been shipped to backers.

Between the end of the Kickstarter campaign and Altar II shipping to backers, Altar II will be available for preorder for $329.

faq.q: Which layouts are available for Altar II? Is there a French, German, Nordic, or other language layout available?
faq.a: Altar II comes in English ANSI (US) and English ISO (UK) only. You will have the opportunity to choose your layout in the survey we send out closer to shipping.
Altar II uses a Mac layout (Command, Option, Control and fn) and there are no Windows keycaps available. Altar II still works as a standard keyboard on Windows.

faq.q: Is there a version with a numpad?
faq.a: Altar II doesn't have a numpad, and we have no plans for a version with one.
Altar II's keycaps are not removable or swappable.

updates.title: 4,250% in 24 hours
updates.text:
I’m incredibly excited to say that Altar II is 4,250% funded just 24 hours after launching on Kickstarter. In that time we’ve raised over $570,000, with over 2,000 backers. To say this has exceeded expectations would be a huge understatement.
After working on Altar II for two years, it was all funded in less than five minutes. It’s scary sharing something that you’ve been working on for so long, especially when the product is as opinionated as Altar II. But the response has been incredible and hugely rewarding to witness.

updates.title: Thank you: Funded in under 5 minutes
updates.text:
Just a few hours into the campaign, Altar II has raised over 2,000% of our goal. We met our funding target in under five minutes.
This is EMO®’s biggest launch day ever: the number of backers who pledged for an Altar II today is more than all the Altar I keyboards sold in its entire production run. Demand has wildly exceeded our expectations, and the team and I thank you from the bottom of our hearts.
